messages:
lee: quick follow-up from the midnight outage postmortem. want to lock down owners for SLO changes and dashboard work before next week.

nina: brief recap pls? I was AFK.

omar: summary: short autoscale gap + long-tail requests from a small group of customers caused p95 to hit ~500ms for ~12m; p99 peaked at 1.6s. availability unaffected but error-budget for our internal latency SLO burned ~18%.

lee: thanks. two threads here: 1) update internal SLOs + error budget calc to reflect observed tail behavior, 2) create detection + mitigation so recurrence is easier to catch.

henry: +1. I'd like the SLO change to be internal-only for 45 days, then we decide on any SLA text change. keeps customers stable.

lee: proposed SLO deltas:
- latency SLO (serving path): p50 < 50ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 750ms (internal)
- autoscale success SLO: 99.8% of required scale-ups succeed within 60s
- throughput SLO (tier-1): target burstable 1800 RPS, steady 1100 RPS
- create a "protective" SLO: when seq-length > baseline+2sd, throttle to protect latency (internal-only)

nina: curious about error-budget math for the autoscale SLO. do we convert failed scale events into time-based burn?

omar: suggested approach: convert each scale-event failure into equivalent downtime using our internal latency SLO. e.g., a 10m window with p95 > target = X% of daily budget. I'll draft formula.

inc-bot: Incident #2024-118 recorded: autoscale latency spike. Severity S2. Postmortem link: https://intranet.redwood/postmortems/2024-118

lee: action items (owners + dates):
- T1: SLO docs & error-budget formula update - owner: @nina - due: 2024-04-22
- T2: Dashboards: add "autoscale event duration" + "error-budget burn by release" panels - owner: @omar - due: 2024-04-18
- T3: Alerts: add burn-rate alert when error-budget consumed >50% in 7d - owner: @henry - due: 2024-04-20
- T4: Runbook: add rapid mitigation steps and rollbacks for autoscale gap - owner: @lee - due: 2024-04-16
- T5: Rate-limiter PoC: implement seq-len protective throttle (internal flag) - owner: @infra - tracked by @omar - due: 2024-05-01
- T6: Customer comms plan (if public SLA text changes) - owner: @prod-comms - due: 2024-05-10

henry: ack T3. I'll add synthetic checks for the slow tail too.

omar: drafting dashboard PR: will include a burn-rate heatmap tied to deployments and pod restarts. linking in the thread when ready.

nina: starting SLO doc PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-slos/pull/92 (WIP)

lee: quick ask on metrics collection: ensure we tag autoscale-trigger events with deploy-tag and request-seqlen bucket. helps correlate.

omar: will add seqlen buckets: small/medium/large and tag events.

henry: for alerts, prefer a two-stage approach: page on >80% burn in 24h, slack-only on 50% in 7d. avoids pager fatigue.

lee: agreed. also schedule follow-up checkpoints:
- checkpoint #1: 1 week (status on dashboards + PRs)
- checkpoint #2: 30 days (internal SLO review, evaluate error-budget behavior)
- checkpoint #3: 60 days (decide public SLA changes if any)

prod-comms: noted. we'll prepare a template for customer messaging but hold until 30d review per agreed process.

inc-bot: Reminder scheduled: Follow-up checkpoint in 7 days for Incident #2024-118.

lee: final note: recurring pattern detection. @omar to run a 90d query to look for similar tail events around batch windows and tag results. if >3 matches, escalate to a retro on operational changes.

omar: on it. I'll post findings in #eng-sre and attach CSV.

nina: thanks all. will merge SLO PR once CI is green and add example burn calculation in the doc.

lee: closing for now. ping this thread with updates and mark tasks done in the follow-up tracker repo. :white_check_mark:
